findings.explanation: HPE documents the HPE Multi-Array Storage vCenter plug-in and HPE GreenLake for Private Cloud Business Edition as the dHCI management interfaces. OneView is not the dHCI control plane, and there is no OneView dHCI resource tree to poll. The whole OneView collection path (hpe:oneview:dhci:cluster from /rest/index/resources?category=appliances&filter="dhci") is built on that false premise.
findings.quote: orchestrated from HPE OneView as the dHCI control plane
findings.suggested_fix: Describe dHCI as managed through the vCenter plug-in and Private Cloud Business Edition. Source cluster and fabric state from the array REST API and vCenter, and drop or clearly mark the OneView dHCI feed as optional server-hardware context.

findings.explanation: The REST API on Alletra 5000/6000 and Nimble arrays (the arrays dHCI uses) is https://<array>:5392/v1/<object_set>, not /api/v1/. The documented object sets (volumes, pools, volume_collections, replication_partners, events) do not include a per-object /perf endpoint.
findings.quote: hpe:alletra:array:perf from GET /api/v1/arrays/{id}/perf; hpe:alletra:volume:perf from GET /api/v1/volumes/{id}/perf
findings.suggested_fix: Use https://<array>:5392/v1/... paths. Take the performance fields from the documented volume and array objects, or from HPE InfoSight/DSCC exports, and state which object carries each latency field.

findings.explanation: Splunkbase app 5380 is 'Mattermost Alerts', not a VMware add-on. The grounding guide lists Splunk Add-on for VMware as 3215, and VMware Metrics is 5089 (Splunk_TA_vmware_inframon). The same wrong ID appears in dataSources, detailedImplementation, and references.
findings.quote: install Splunk Add-on for VMware vSphere (Splunkbase 5380, folder Splunk_TA_vmware)
findings.suggested_fix: Replace 5380 with the correct add-on, either Splunk Add-on for VMware (3215, Splunk_TA_vmware) or Splunk Add-on for VMware Metrics (5089, Splunk_TA_vmware_inframon), in every field. Fix the reference title and URL to match.

findings.explanation: HPE QuickSpecs list the dHCI storage as one HPE Nimble Storage, Alletra 6000, or Alletra 5000 array. Alletra 9000 is not a dHCI array. The same claim repeats in detailedImplementation.
findings.quote: a paired HPE Alletra 5000, 6000, or 9000 controller stack
findings.suggested_fix: Limit supported arrays to Nimble, Alletra 5000, and Alletra 6000 in hardware and detailedImplementation.

findings.explanation: The description's thresholds are guard conditions lifted from eval statements. The SPL actually grades severity on latency_drift_pct (above 20, 50, 100, or 200 percent), p95 above 5000 microseconds, pool_used_pct above 60, 80, or 90, RPO breaches, and fabric_down. controlTest repeats the same wrong thresholds.
findings.suggested_fix: Have the description and controlTest state the real severity ladder from the SPL's sev0 case statement.

findings.explanation: The Splunk Add-on for VMware documents datastore performance as vmware:perf:datastore and vCenter events as vmware:events (vmware_inframon:* in the Metrics add-on). Neither vmware:perf nor vmware:vc:event exists, and read_latency_ms and write_latency_ms are not add-on field names.
findings.quote: index=vmware sourcetype vmware:perf from Splunk Add-on for VMware vSphere ... for ESXi read_latency_ms and write_latency_ms on datastores, cross-checked in microseconds in the search; optional vmware:vc:event for APD/PDL
findings.suggested_fix: Use vmware:perf:datastore with its documented counter fields, and use vmware:events for APD/PDL, in dataSources, app, detailedImplementation, and visualization.

findings.explanation: OneView REST sessions return a sessionID, which is sent in the 'Auth' header along with 'X-API-Version'. X-API-Key is not the OneView pattern.
findings.quote: for OneView, follow login-session then X-API-Key patterns your appliance documents
findings.suggested_fix: Check the HPE OneView REST API reference and describe the Auth and X-API-Version headers.

findings.explanation: This is authoring meta-commentary, as is 'This validation trail is not the oVirt or Proxmox story from sibling 19.2 UCs'. Neither helps the implementer.
findings.quote: This document is the first cat-19.2 dHCI/Alletra use case. It does not import vSAN or Nutanix multisearch field contracts from sibling UCs

findings.explanation: dhci_tier_key is never produced by the SPL, so throttling will not work as described. The suggestion to set dispatch.ttl to cut SmartStore re-scan cost is also not how dispatch.ttl works; it controls how long search artifacts are kept.
findings.suggested_fix: Suppress on cluster_name,tier, and remove the SmartStore dispatch.ttl advice.

findings.explanation: The HEC link is truncated to a directory, the OneView link points to the opensource.hpe.com homepage, and the Alletra link is a marketing page. None of them leads to the API pages the UC depends on.
findings.suggested_fix: Cite the HEC page (Data/UsetheHTTPEventCollector), the Nimble/Alletra REST API reference on support.hpe.com, the dHCI deployment guide, and the OneView REST API reference.

findings.explanation: The UC is marked verified by a generic reviewer handle, yet it contains wrong product architecture, API paths, and Splunkbase IDs, so no SME validation is evident.
findings.suggested_fix: Set the status to draft or community until an SME validates it against a live dHCI system.

firewalled_field_flags.issue: Pool oversubscription normalisation is inverted. The eval `pool_oversub=if(po>1.0, po/100, po)` turns a real overcommit ratio such as 1.5 into 0.015, while under-committed ratios below 1 pass through unchanged and trigger the critical branch (pool_oversub>0.9). The pool_used_pct arm also mixes volume provisioned_bytes with pool rows, so it is not pool utilisation.

The title promises per-tier latency, but stats rolls up BY cluster_name only. Joining dhci_latency_baseline with max=0 then fans each cluster's single p95 out to every tier, so latency_drift_pct per tier compares one cluster-wide number against several tier baselines.

`latest(fabric_link_state)` runs across all arms, and most arms hard-code "unknown", so a real 'down' from the OneView arm can be masked by a later perf event. The hpe:alletra:event arm also marks any warning severity, or any _raw containing the substrings sas, fan, psu, chap, or ntp, as array_fault=1, which forces a critical severity and will over-page.

The ESXi arm searches sourcetype="vmware:perf" with read_latency_ms and write_latency_ms. The Splunk Add-on for VMware emits vmware:perf:datastore with counter-named fields, so this arm will return nothing as written.

The search has no `where severity_bucket!="ok"` filter, yet implementation tells the reader the alert should trigger only on non-ok rows (troubleshooting item l admits this). As written, the scheduled alert fires every run.

summary: The UC has a lot of detail, but its architecture is wrong. It treats HPE OneView as the dHCI control plane, uses the wrong REST paths for Alletra 5000/6000 arrays, and cites Splunkbase 5380 as the VMware add-on even though that ID is an unrelated alerting app. Template residue in the description and false-positive text, plus SPL math bugs, make it worse.
